title: Boiler on solar panels
excerpt: There is a wide range of endurance devices. In this blog you can read about the pros and cons per technology and the best option for you!
contentHtml:
Wide range of endurance devices

It is becoming increasingly important for solar panel owners to be able to use their own generated solar energy themselves. Without a netting scheme, being able to use idle solar energy is not only more sustainable, but also cost effective. Moreover, it is increasingly common for the low-voltage grid to become overloaded because too many households in a district supply power back. When this happens, the inverter can turn off, preventing the solar panels from producing power temporarily. That must change. Now there are several technologies that can use extra solar energy. This wide range can make it difficult to determine what works best for different households. That is why here is an overview of a number of comparable technologies to explain the operation, advantages and disadvantages of each option. The technologies that are compared are:

  • WaterAccu
  • Heat pump boiler
  • solar water heater
  • home battery

How exactly does each technology work?

WaterAccu

The WaterAccu consists of an electric boiler and a smart box, the Solar iBoost. The iBoost knows when power is supplied to the grid via a measuring clamp in the meter box. The iBoost then activates the boiler so that the excess power can be used to heat the water in the boiler. More efficient use of own power, and it saves gas.

View the water accu

Heat pump boiler

The heat pump boiler also has the function to heat tap water. However, this device hardly works with electrical elements. The primary heating source is a heat exchanger built into a buffer tank. This extracts heat from the environment to heat the water. This system works very efficiently, but takes a relatively long time to heat water.

solar water heater

Solar water heaters are also used to heat tap water. However, unlike the first two technologies, a solar water heater does not work on electricity. Instead, a solar water heater uses a so-called solar collector to absorb heat from the sun. This heat is transported to a buffer tank via a heat exchanger to heat the tap water. This therefore ensures lower gas and electricity consumption.

home battery

The home battery is the only technology out of four that is not specifically designed to heat tap water. Instead, solar power is stored in a battery. This current can be used later by other electrical appliances, usually when the sun is not shining

What are the advantages and disadvantages per technology?

Both WaterAccu and heat pump boiler have the advantage that they reduce gas consumption and improve the use of their own electricity. The efficiency of the heat pump boiler is higher, making it function better without sun. However, the WaterAccu can make more use of peaks in solar energy, which helps to avoid peak loads.

The biggest advantage of the solar water heater is that this technology does not depend on solar panels. However, the solar water heater collector takes up a lot of space, which means that it will not always be possible to combine a solar water heater with solar panels.

Finally, the home battery offers more options for using the stored power, but there are relatively high costs. A home battery quickly costs around 6000 euros, while the costs for the other technologies are usually between 1500 and 3000 euros. This can therefore be a significant obstacle to purchase.

What is best for me?

With so many options, it is so nice to know what best suits your personal situation. Of the four options, the WaterAccu and the heat pump boiler are most similar. The choice between them therefore depends on small differences. If a household suffers a lot from peak loads, the WaterAccu works better. However, if little idle solar energy is available, the higher efficiency of the heat pump boiler offers an advantage. A solar water heater is relatively favorable for a household without solar panels, although this may also hinder a possible later purchase of solar panels. If money does not play a role and a lot of unused energy is available, the home battery can also be a good investment.
